# Demo day readiness: the meeting on Tuesday 06.10.2026 Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** By the meeting with a Slovenian EPC on Tuesday 06.10.2026, Belin is live on its own domain, every screen shown in the meeting works and looks like a finished 2026 product, every document it produces is correct, the founder can play every role in one tap, and the buyer can sign up alone the same evening.

**Architecture:** No rewrite. The audit found a good product hidden behind three dead infrastructure services, a layer of visible bugs, demo data that lies, and a missing front door. The plan fixes in that order: infrastructure, demo truth and the presenter door, correctness of the paths the demo walks, self-serve signup, the visual system, documents, the landing page, then a rehearsal with a written run of show. The full plan is about 112 agent hours; tonight's target is the **Minimum winning cut** (about 46 agent hours with gates, four lanes). Everything else is the **Add order**, taken only while the clock is green, and the rest ships after the meeting.

**Tech Stack:** Next.js 15 App Router, React 19, next-intl (sl, de, en), Supabase (Postgres, Storage, Realtime; project xrwncpngjajosstvkign, Frankfurt), Vercel (project belin-app, prj_v40d8vMzjATWstV7Y8bs43A9swth), Resend, @react-pdf/renderer 4, vitest, Playwright (scripts only).

**How to read this plan.** Part A says what the audit found. Part B is what the founder does tonight before sleeping (Wave 0, including the approvals that let the night run unattended). Part C is the list of decisions taken on the founder's behalf. Then the execution model, the task index, the Minimum winning cut, the Add and Cut orders and the Clock checkpoints. Then one section per wave with every task in full. Part Z is the definition of done. The audit reports this plan stands on are in `docs/audits/2026-10-05-demo-recon/`.

## Global Constraints

- Audience: a SLOVENIAN EPC, meeting in SLOVENIAN, in person, founder's laptop plus founder's phone. Slovenian copy is the product copy. German and English get real translations only where a task says so; otherwise new keys carry the Slovenian string as a placeholder (founder mandate 2026-07-19), each listed in the task's translation-debt ledger file (index rule 6), and the debt is logged in CHANGELOG.md.
- Pitch is BOTH: AVESOL as the installation subcontractor, and Belin as the product the EPC can roll out to all its subcontractors.
- After the meeting the buyer must be able to SIGN UP ALONE (self-serve EPC signup).
- Never use em dashes (U+2014) or en dashes (U+2013) in any produced text: UI, PDFs, emails, docs, commit messages, chat.
- Every change is logged in CHANGELOG.md in the same commit. Every significant decision gets one line in DECISIONS.md. The executing session writes docs/sessions/2026-10-06-demo-day-execution.md, including the Rollback ledger, the SPEED measurements and the section "Za ustanovitelja zjutraj".
- One database serves local, demo and production (memory: one-database-for-local-and-production). A local dev server reads and writes the PRODUCTION database. `npm run seed` rewrites the live demo. Every migration applied through the Supabase connector gets a matching file in supabase/migrations/ in the same commit (memory: migration-file-with-every-connector-apply). Types are regenerated per index rule 3 (the Supabase connector's generate_typescript_types; `npm run gen:types` cannot run on this machine).
- Do not run `npm run build` while a dev server is running in the same folder: both use `.next`. Build in a separate worktree (`git worktree add ../belin-build HEAD`) or rely on the Vercel build of a pushed commit.
- Pushing main deploys PRODUCTION (belin-app, and getbelin.com once Task 0.3 is done). Push only green commits: `npm test` and `npm run lint` pass first. Only main is pushed; lanes never push branches.
- `git add -A` is forbidden (another session may have files in the tree). Add by path.
- Reference repos C:\DevEnv\Belin 1.0.0 and C:\DevEnv\AVE-DC are read-only.
- Contract-forming acts (PO accept, acceptance signatures, invoice) stay person-only and office-only. Nothing in this plan widens requireOfficeActor.
- A generated document path is written once; regenerating means a new row and a new path (DECISIONS 2026-08-12). Content reads go through cache-busted signed URLs.
- Every PDF render goes through renderDocument in lib/pdf/theme.tsx (DECISIONS 2026-08-12, font subset bug).
- No server component decides what to render from a client-only signal (DECISIONS 2026-08-13, SplashGate hydration bug).
- The in-app preview browser reports document.hidden = true permanently (memory: preview-tab-permanently-hidden). Verify with Playwright, not the preview pane.
- Verify rendered geometry, not containers (memory: verify-rendered-geometry): measure the element that carries the value.
- Look at every screenshot and every PDF page at the size it renders. Filenames and code are not evidence.
- Page views write to the database (index rule 7). No public write surface (index rule 8). One writer on the demo at a time (index rule 11).
- After 23:30 no gate waits for the founder. Anything only he can check goes to the session log section "Za ustanovitelja zjutraj" and is walked through at the 08:00 checkpoint.

## Rollback plan (production)

Facts read 05.10.2026 about 22:30 through the Vercel connector:
- Team team_lrl4KQuxHhBQlJKlfcwqNBcE. Project belin-app: prj_v40d8vMzjATWstV7Y8bs43A9swth.
- Production now: dpl_EUTbu612Gd87sZXHnj1JSctgqmL5 (commit e89f2de, region iad1, built in 72 s). Previous: dpl_8m2rZQxY2GUamGzzCF5D7dijUT1B (f03c751).
- On Hobby, Instant Rollback reaches only the immediately previous production deployment.

**R0, 23:00, before any commit:**
```bash
git tag -a demo-eve-start e89f2de -m "production before the demo night: dpl_EUTbu612Gd87sZXHnj1JSctgqmL5"
git push origin demo-eve-start
```
The session log gets a table "Rollback ledger" with columns: tag | sha | deployment id | contains | safe to show. After every push that reaches READY, the orchestrator reads the id with the Vercel connector list_deployments (project belin-app, target production, limit 1), then runs `git tag -a <tag> <sha> -m "<deployment id>"` and `git push origin <tag>`, and adds a row.
- demo-eve-start: still shows the leaked landing images. Use only before 7.1 is live.
- demo-safe-floor: the 7.1 deployment, the floor for anything public.
- gate-1-2: the first deployment with the Door. This is the meeting floor.
- gate-3, gate-4.
- demo-freeze: written at 11:45.

**How:**
1. Immediately previous deployment: Vercel connector request_rollback (project prj_v40d8vMzjATWstV7Y8bs43A9swth, deployment id from the ledger). No rebuild. Then `curl -sI` the host `/sl` and run the Door smoke.
2. Further back: request_promote with the ledger id. If Hobby refuses, restore the tree and push a new commit:
```bash
git restore --source=gate-1-2 --staged --worktree -- .
git diff --cached --stat
git commit -m "revert: production back to the gate-1-2 tree"
git push origin main
```
   Expect READY in about two minutes. Never force-push main.
3. The database is never rolled back. Tonight's migrations are additive or keep the old call shape, so every ledger deployment runs on the new schema (checked at each apply, risk R6). Never run `npm run seed` from a tree older than gate-1-2: the old seed writes Sonce Energija and AVESOL's real rate back.
4. Env vars stay as they are; every ledger deployment tolerates them.

**When:**
- Before 12:00: a gate push whose production smoke fails and is not fixed within 20 minutes rolls back to the previous ledger row. The fix continues on a branch.
- 12:00 to the meeting: nothing is pushed. If a founder-approved blocker fix breaks anything, Instant Rollback to FREEZE_ID at once. If the freeze build itself regresses in the rehearsal, the founder may promote gate-3 or gate-1-2, and the run of show uses the fallbacks of the features after that gate.
- During the meeting: never. Use fallback ladder step 4 (offline kit).
- The cheat sheet (Task 9.4) prints FREEZE_ID and gate-3's id.

- **R10. Laptop capacity** (31.7 GB RAM, 17.8 GB free, 12 threads, 56.6 GB disk free, read 05.10 22:30). Guard: at most three `next dev` servers at once (stop an idle lane's server). The build worktree runs only while at most two dev servers run. Stop a lane's dev server before `npm ci` in it (Windows EPERM).
- **R11. Competing placeholder mechanisms.** Guard: 1.4a in the prelude; only `tests/translation-debt/<task-id>.json` is used (index rule 6).

- **R13. Screenshot review floods the orchestrator.** Guard: each lane looks at its own screenshots and writes one sentence each in its own section of the session log. The orchestrator looks only at gate sweeps.

Gate tests, the founder's logins, the buyer's signup and every notification share it. Guard: Task 0.10; no script sends email in a loop; the Wave 8 email task stays cut unless the cap is lifted.

## Part A: what the audit found, in plain language

Twelve read-only auditors went through the product on the evening of 05.10.2026: the landing page, the EPC side, the subcontractor and crew side on phones, every PDF, the database and deploys, the language catalogs, the design system, the spec against the code, the server code paths, the meeting itself, the market and a list of ideas. Their full reports are in the planning session's scratch folder; the facts that drive this plan are below.

**Found broken tonight, outside the code (none of these would have been noticed before the meeting):**

1. **The database was paused.** Supabase pauses a free project after seven quiet days. Every page that reads data, on the live site and on the laptop, showed "Povezava ni veljavna". It was resumed at 19:13 UTC on 05.10 with the founder's approval. It will pause again after the next quiet week unless Task 0.1 and Task 1.8 are done.
2. **No email can be sent.** The sending domain getbelin.com lost its DKIM record at Hostinger, so Resend marks it failed. Login links, invitations, notifications and the accountant share all fail silently while the screen says "sent". The live site has no other way in.
3. **getbelin.com shows the old Belin 1.0.0 site**, with invented customer logos ("Trusted by solar companies across Europe"), invented numbers and a different price list. That domain is printed on every PDF footer, every email and the brochure.
4. **Functions run in Washington (iad1)** against a Frankfurt database. Every click crosses the Atlantic several times, and "Podatki v EU, Frankfurt" is only half true.
5. **Hosting plans:** Vercel Hobby forbids commercial use; Supabase Free has no backups. Fine for one meeting, not for a paying customer.
6. **Your other two Supabase projects (`solarflow-crm`, `avesol`) are paused too.** If avesol.si's contact form uses the `avesol` project, that form is down. Unverified; worth one look.

**Found in what the buyer would see:**

7. **The public landing page shows a real private customer's name and home address** (from a real K2 plan: Planung Engelmeier, Oberlaaer Str. 88, 1100 Wien) in the wizard screenshot. That is a GDPR problem on the exact page an EPC uses to judge how you handle data.
8. **The demo client is a real Slovenian company, Sonce Energija d.o.o.**, a ZSFV member your own GTM notes forbid showing. It is on the landing page's document images and on every generated document. A Slovenian EPC will likely know them. The same documents print AVESOL's real price (118.500 EUR for 245,7 kWp and 48 EUR/h), which hands the buyer your rate in a meeting where you also sell AVESOL.
9. **The demo data is seven weeks old.** The "current" project's last report is from August, the hour sheet countdown has run out, and the expiring certificate has expired.
10. **There is no way to be the EPC, the subcontractor office and the crew on the live site.** The demo addresses are fake and never receive mail; the old 12345 login only creates link sessions, which cannot open the naročilnica, approve hours, or reach Zaključek. The closing beats of the runbook were never possible from it.
11. **Self-serve signup does not exist.** No code path creates an EPC customer. The login form tells a stranger "link sent" and sends nothing.
12. **Projects created from a K2 plan can never show progress.** The wizard creates no progress items, so the project sits at 0 % forever and the crew form has no quantities. It also stores no coordinates, so no weather ever attaches. The demo hides this because the seed hand-writes both. A buyer who signs up and uploads a plan meets exactly this.
13. **The AVESOL boss cannot accept an invitation from a new EPC.** An existing subcontractor gets "email already used". The buyer inviting AVESOL to their first real project fails.

**Found on screen (from screenshots, a CSS harness and code):**

14. The subcontractor's home is visibly broken: every card label escapes its card and piles up at the bottom left, and "Čaka na vas" always says "Naročilnice še ni" even when one is waiting. The boss's "Dnevno poročanje" button leads to a sign-up form and back to the same page.
15. On the crew report screen the "Odjava" pill sits on top of "Pošlji poročilo". The incident and request sheets open underneath the tab bar. Marking material "Delno" widens the page sideways, and that is the runbook's day-one demo step. Quantities only move in steps of 10 and cannot be typed. A typical report takes about 33 taps.
16. Portfolio tiles read "1 MWp4 zaključeni projekti". Status chips stretch into bars. Numbers print "58.3" and "245.7 kWp" with English decimals next to "6,5". The hero shows two different tempo numbers (5.9 and 6,5). The "v živo" badge floats outside the page. Approve and reject sit at different heights. There is no favicon and every tab has the same title. A 4.5 second logo animation plays on every page load and every language switch.
17. On the live (production) build, every specific error message from the server is replaced by React with a generic one, so ten screens show "conflict" when the real problem is "tick the declaration" or "add a VAT number".
18. There are no loading screens and no error pages. A slow database looks like a dead click; a failed query says "this link was revoked".

**Found in the documents:**

19. Every paragraph prints double spaced (a line-height bug, six lines of code).
20. The invoice lacks fields the VAT law requires: both parties' addresses and the date or period of supply (82. člen ZDDV-1, § 14 Abs. 4 UStG). It also lacks a due date, which the VAT law does not require but every accountant expects.
21. The naročilnica says it was accepted ten days before it was issued.
22. The completion report counts rejected and pending hours, so its total disagrees with the invoice.
23. Day pages never name the project, crop portrait photos to strips, and can push the signature alone onto a new page.
24. The Zapisnik o prevzemu allows a warranty start before the acceptance and a refusal with no defects; defect photos never reach the PDF.
25. The signature pad uploads on every stroke to one fixed path; per the repo's own known-issues, the protocol most likely prints only the first stroke.
26. Belin's name sits where the issuing company's should be: AVESOL's invoice looks Belin-issued.

**The good news, also verified:** 431 tests pass, types are clean, the reverse-charge logic is right for SI, DE and AT, totals add up, every diacritic renders, the PO hash binding and the transactional report submit are sound, and the dark and gold design is strong. What reads as "not professional" is a layer of fixable bugs and inconsistency, not the design direction. No redesign is needed; a system pass is.

## Execution model

**One orchestrator, four lanes.** The executing session (Opus) is the orchestrator. It dispatches one subagent per lane (superpowers:subagent-driven-development) and does not execute lane tasks itself. It owns `main`, migrations, type regeneration, seeds, pushes, gates and the Rollback ledger.

- Lane A is the main worktree `C:\DevEnv\belin-app` on :3000.
- Lanes B, C and D are worktrees: `git worktree add ../belin-lane-<x> -b lane-<x> main`, then `cp .env.local ../belin-lane-<x>/.env.local` and set `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=http://localhost:300<n>` in that copy, then `npm ci` and `npx next dev -p 300<n>`. B is :3001, C is :3002, D is :3003.
- B and D are created at 23:15 from the 1.1 commit (7.1, 1.11 and 4.2 need nothing else). C is created at 00:30 from main after the prelude (1.4a, 2.1a, 1.3, 1.2), because the Door builds on 1.2's session cache and 2.1a's flag.
- After any merge of main that changed package-lock.json, the lane stops its dev server, runs `npm ci`, and restarts it.
- **Package rule:** package.json dependencies and package-lock.json change tonight only in the prelude (1.3) or in lane C (2.3b `qrcode`, 5.1a `lucide-react` and `sonner`, 3.4 moves `sharp` to dependencies). Any other lane that needs a package asks the orchestrator.
- **Gate 1 and Gate 2 run as one gate, Gate 1+2** (Tasks 1.12 and 2.6 in that order). Merge order: A, D, B, then C up to tag `lane-c-door` (end of 2.3c), push, Door smoke on production; then the rest of C (2.4) and push.
- **Conflict rule for app/actions/auth.ts and app/[locale]/login/page.tsx:** keep lane C's deletion of loginAction, LoginForm and demoLoginEnabled (2.4); keep lane A's other 1.7 changes (rate limit, exact email lookups, safeNext); delete tests/auth-login-gate.test.ts.
- **Wave 3:** 3.1a runs on main right after Gate 1+2 and the orchestrator applies its two migrations. Then streams run in parallel: A (3.1b, 3.2, 3.5), B (3.7, then 3.3), C (3.4). The e2e scripts of different streams never run at the same time (rule 11).
- **No extra worktrees.** Only lanes A to D exist, on :3000 to :3003. Where a section describes its own extra worktree, track or stream port (Wave 3 streams, Wave 5 tracks A1 and A2, Wave 8), map it onto the lane this index assigns and use that lane's port; never create a fifth dev server.
- **Dates and numbers on screen and paper go through lib/format.ts (Task 1.11).** Where a section formats with its own Intl call or next-intl's useFormatter (3.7 PoView, Wave 6's lib/pdf/doc-format.ts, some Wave 8 tasks), the executor routes it through lib/format.ts so every date reads the same way; Wave 6's doc helpers delegate to lib/format.ts instead of re-implementing it.
- **Merging:** `git merge --no-ff lane-<x>`. CHANGELOG.md, messages/*.json and package.json conflicts are resolved by keeping both sides, then adding the missing comma between the two appended blocks (each side ends its block without one), then checking that `node -e "for (const f of ['messages/sl.json','messages/de.json','messages/en.json','package.json']) JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync(f,'utf8'))"` prints nothing. A package-lock.json conflict is never merged by hand: `git checkout --ours package-lock.json`, stop the dev server, `npm install`, `git add package-lock.json`. Then `npm test` and `npm run lint`, push, and check the Vercel deployment.

**Shared-file rules, so merges stay trivial:**

1. `messages/sl.json`, `de.json`, `en.json`: a task adds keys only inside the namespace its task header names. A new namespace is appended at the END of the file. Editing an existing key's text is allowed only in the task that owns that namespace (the ownership list below).
2. `app/globals.css`: Wave 5 owns every existing rule. Any other wave appends its rules inside its own block at the end of the file, opened with a comment line `/* === <task id>: <title> === */`, and never edits rules above it.
3. **Migrations and types.** Each lane writes its migration FILE; only the orchestrator applies it (apply_migration on xrwncpngjajosstvkign), one at a time, in the order of the task index, then regenerates types ON MAIN with the Supabase connector `generate_typescript_types`, writing its complete output to lib/database.types.ts (`npm run gen:types` cannot run here: the CLI is not linked). After every regeneration, restore the one deliberate hand edit: in `Functions.create_project_from_review.Args`, `p_roofs: Json` (and `p_scope: Json` once 4.5a is applied) are required, with the comment block above them; verify with `grep -n "p_roofs: Json$" lib/database.types.ts`. Commit it alone (`chore(types): regenerate after <migration names>`). When migrations from two lanes land together (for example 3.1a's two files with 4.1's), apply them back to back and regenerate once. Lanes never edit lib/database.types.ts; on a conflict in it during a merge or rebase, take main's version and regenerate.
4. `npm run seed` is run only by the orchestrator, only on main, only at a gate (or in Task 9.4).
5. CHANGELOG.md: every task commit adds its lines under a heading `## 2026-10-06` at the top. On merge conflict keep both.
6. **Translation debt, one mechanism for every wave.** `tests/messages-parity.test.ts` ("carry no Slovenian left over in de or en") fails on any de or en value equal to the Slovenian one. Task 1.4a (Wave 1, in the prelude) adds the ledger: one JSON file per task, `tests/translation-debt/<task-id>-<namespace>.json`, listing the full keys (no locale prefix) that knowingly carry Slovenian in de and en; the test skips them and fails on a listed key that is already translated or does not exist. Procedure for any task: add the keys to all three catalogs, run `npm test -- tests/messages-parity.test.ts`, write exactly the keys it reports into the task's ledger file, rerun until green. No task other than 1.4a edits tests/messages-parity.test.ts, and no other exemption list, prefix list or namespace exemption exists.
7. **Page views write to the database** (LF12): dashboards persist deemed approvals and send reminder rows on render. Every rehearsal and every agent walk can consume the demo countdown. The final reseed (Task 9.4) runs after the last rehearsal and after 00:00 UTC on Tuesday, and preflight re-checks the open hour sheet just before the meeting.
8. **No public write surface.** The EPC token page `/p/[token]` can add material lines and change status, so no public "live project" link or QR is published on the landing, in onboarding, in emails, or anywhere else. Live proof on the landing is a silent loop or still pictures.
9. **Marketing shots never show demo chrome or the personalized name.** The DemoPersonaBar hides under the `belin-shot` cookie (lib/shot-mode.ts). Every public asset is shot from the invented identity BEFORE Task 9.4 personalizes the demo with the buyer's name.
10. **Real names are renamed by id, not by name.** Task 2.2 renames the demo EPC and every real brand in the demo portfolio (PSE Lidl Domžale, Hala Trimo Trebnje, Streha Gorenje Velenje, and any real subcontractor names). Tests and scripts refer to demo projects and orgs by their fixed UUIDs, never by display name.
11. **One writer on the demo at a time, and quiet windows.** Any command that writes demo data or revokes demo sessions takes the lock first: `npm run seed`, `seed:documents`, `scripts/e2e/*.mjs`, any `scripts/qa/check-*.mjs` that submits, the Wave 4 test-organization recipe, `marketing:*` pipelines, `demo-door-smoke`, and any Wave 8 verification that writes. PowerShell: `New-Item C:\DevEnv\belin-db.lock -ItemType File -Value "<lane> <task> <HH:MM>"` (fails if the file exists). Git Bash: `set -o noclobber; echo "<lane> <task> $(date +%H:%M)" > /c/DevEnv/belin-db.lock`. Delete the file when done. If the lock exists, the lane waits (Monitor until the file is gone) and does read-only work meanwhile. During a gate, and while the orchestrator runs a marketing pipeline (7.2a, 7.2b, 9.3a) or a reseed, it holds the lock for a QUIET WINDOW: nothing else signs in to or writes to the demo, no Playwright verification runs, nobody clicks through the demo; lanes keep coding and run only `npm test` and `npm run lint`. The orchestrator writes each window's start and end into the session log. A local dev server reads and writes the production database, so "on localhost" never exempts a step. After any reseed every lane re-enters through the Door before its next Playwright run. A lock older than 30 minutes is reported to the orchestrator, never deleted by another lane.

**Gates.** A gate is passed when: `npm test` passes, `npm run lint` passes, the branches are merged and pushed, the Vercel production deployment for that commit is READY (Vercel connector `list_deployments` or `get_deployment`), and the gate's smoke checks pass on production. The orchestrator writes the result, the clock time and a Rollback ledger row into the session log. **Gates never wait for the founder.** A line marked (F) is recorded as pending, with the connector evidence (for example Resend get-email status delivered), in the session log section "Za ustanovitelja zjutraj", and the founder confirms it at the 08:00 checkpoint or the rehearsal.

## Task index

Priorities: P0 = the meeting fails without it. P1 = it looks like a real professional product. P2 = the surprise. Effort is agent hours from each task's own section header (the section headers are authoritative for EFFORT; SPEED is computed from them). "MIN" marks the Minimum winning cut.

**Precedence.** Where a wave section's own overview disagrees with this index on order, lane, timing, priority or whether a task runs tonight, THIS INDEX, the Minimum winning cut, the Add and Cut orders and the Clock checkpoints win. The sections are authoritative for HOW a task is done. Id aliases: 1.8L is "Task 1.8 lite" in the Wave 1 section; 1.4a is the prelude part of Task 1.4; 5.1a and 5.1b are the two parts of Task 5.1; 6.1m is defined at the top of the Wave 6 section.

## Wave 1: Stabilise

Wave 1 makes the live product safe to stand on before anything is built on top of it: functions move to Frankfurt, Next.js leaves the RCE advisories behind, a database hiccup stops saying "link revoked", server errors reach the screen in production, the 4.5 s splash leaves the browser, the security holes close before strangers get accounts, a daily cron keeps the free database awake (it takes over the clocks on Wednesday 07.10, see Task 1.8), email stops lying about delivery, signed photos stop expiring, and one formatter exists for numbers and dates.

Prelude on main (23:15 to 00:30): 1.1, then the 1.4a block of Task 1.4 alone (commit `test(i18n): translation-debt ledger`), then Wave 2's 2.1a, then 1.3, then 1.2. Lane A (main) after the prelude: 1.5, 1.9, 1.7, 1.10. Lane D (worktree belin-lane-d, :3003): 1.11 from 23:15, then 1.6 and 1.8 lite. The rest of 1.4 (error, loading, not found) is Add order item 4. Gate 1 (1.12) runs together with Gate 2 (2.6) as Gate 1+2.

How the lanes are set up and why the order holds (adapted to the two lanes above):
- Prelude and lane A work in `C:\DevEnv\belin-app` on `main`, dev server on port 3000. Lane D is created the same way as the other lanes (01-index, Execution model), as soon as 1.1 is committed (a few minutes after 23:15), so it carries the `## 2026-10-06` CHANGELOG heading that 1.1 creates:
  ```bash
  git worktree add ../belin-lane-d -b lane-d main
  cp .env.local ../belin-lane-d/.env.local
  cd ../belin-lane-d && npm ci && npx next dev -p 3003
  ```
- "Add order item 4" means: the rest of 1.4 leaves Gate 1 and runs in lane A after Gate 1+2, as the fourth item of the add order in the timeline. If the timeline carries no add order, it runs in lane A directly after Gate 1+2, before Wave 3 starts.
- The order matters in these places: 1.3 before every production-build check; 1.5 before 1.9 (both edit `components/final/InvoiceCard.tsx` and `lib/data/invoices.ts`); 1.9 before 1.7 (both edit `app/actions/auth.ts` and `app/[locale]/p/[token]/claim-actions.ts`); 1.8 lite needs `vercel.json` from 1.2 and `emailFrom()` and `senderDomain()` from 1.9, so lane D merges `main` before those steps (Task 1.8 says when).
- Lane D's tasks touch no lane A file except CHANGELOG.md, DECISIONS.md, the end of `app/globals.css` and `vercel.json` (taken from main by a merge before it is edited). The orchestrator merges lane D into main with `git merge --no-ff lane-d` before Gate 1+2; conflicts in CHANGELOG.md, DECISIONS.md and the CSS tail are resolved by keeping both sides.

Gate: Task 1.12, run together with Gate 2 (Task 2.6) as Gate 1+2, after lane D is merged. `npm test` and `npm run lint` green, the migration of 1.7 applied, production READY on `fra1`, `/api/health` green, the cron answering, the founder's login email reported delivered by Resend (his own look at his inbox is on the morning list and never blocks the gate or the next wave), D1 to D20 in DECISIONS.md.

### Conventions for every Wave 1 task (read once)

- **Commit**: add files BY PATH, never `git add -A`. Each commit carries its CHANGELOG.md lines under one `## 2026-10-06` heading at the top of the file (Task 1.1 creates the heading; later tasks add bullets under it). The executor appends its own attribution lines to every commit message as its session instructions say. No em or en dashes anywhere, commit messages included.
- **Push**: lane A is `main`, and pushing `main` deploys PRODUCTION. Push only after `npm test` and `npm run lint` pass. Tasks 1.2, 1.3 and 1.8 must be pushed to be verified; the others may wait for the gate.
- **The build worktree** (production build without touching the dev server's `.next`): created once in Task 1.3 at `C:\DevEnv\belin-build`. To refresh it for a later check:
  ```bash
  git -C C:/DevEnv/belin-build checkout --detach main
  cd C:/DevEnv/belin-build && npm ci && npm run build
  ```
  (`npm ci` only when package-lock.json changed since the last build.) Start it with `npx next start -p 3005` using the Bash tool's `run_in_background`, stop it when done. Never run `npm run build` inside `C:\DevEnv\belin-app`.
- **Windows trap**: stop the dev server before any `npm install` or `npm ci` in `C:\DevEnv\belin-app`. The running server holds `@next/swc-win32-x64-msvc/*.node` open and npm fails with EPERM. Restart it afterwards with `npm run dev` in the background.
- **Shared database**: the dev server, the build worktree and production all read Supabase `xrwncpngjajosstvkign`. Nothing in Wave 1 runs `npm run seed`. The verification scripts below write only: one temporary `sessions` row each (deleted after), and the cron's own idempotent work.
- **Throwaway scripts** go in `C:\DevEnv\belin-app\.tmp-qa\` (gitignored), run from the repo root so `playwright` and `@supabase/supabase-js` resolve.
- **Catalog rule**: Wave 1 owns the new `errors` namespace (appended at the END of each of `messages/sl.json`, `de.json`, `en.json`) and one addition to `common` (`common.sendFailed`). The Wave 1 strings are final, so de and en get REAL translations here, not Slovenian placeholders: `tests/messages-parity.test.ts` ("carry no Slovenian left over in de or en") fails on any placeholder. Task 1.4a adds the ledger that lets later waves use placeholders without breaking the gate.
- **CSS rule**: Wave 1 appends two blocks at the end of `app/globals.css` (currently 2897 lines), each opened with its marker comment (`/* === 1.4: ... === */`, `/* === 1.6: ... === */`). No rule above them is edited.
- **The preview pane is always hidden** (document.hidden = true). Every visual check below uses Playwright from `.tmp-qa/`, at 390x844 and 360x740 for anything crew-facing, plus 1440x900. Every screenshot is opened and looked at.

### Where this section disagrees with the recon (checked against code and the live database on 05.10.2026)

- i18n-copy I18N-17 infers that production has `DEMO_LOGIN=1` because the production login HTML contains "Benutzername". Wrong inference: `NextIntlClientProvider` in `app/[locale]/layout.tsx:137` serializes the whole catalog into every page, and `app/[locale]/login/page.tsx:78` renders `LoginForm` only when `DEMO_LOGIN === "1"`. The real hole is DR-M1: `loginAction` itself has no gate and is reachable (fixed in 1.7).
- flows-correctness L3 and backend-ops BO-15 are confirmed LIVE: `material_check_docs` has `relrowsecurity = false` and anon holds INSERT, SELECT, UPDATE, DELETE on it; all four public functions are EXECUTE for anon and authenticated; only `create_project_from_review(uuid,uuid,uuid,jsonb,jsonb,text,text,jsonb)` is SECURITY DEFINER (`search_path=public`).
- New, not in any recon: `requestMagicLink` (`app/actions/auth.ts:74`) and `acceptInvite` (`lib/data/invites.ts:111`) use the same ILIKE wildcard lookup as the crew claim; all six stored emails are lowercase today. `lib/storage.ts:133` and `:158` CACHE an empty map for 50 minutes when signing fails once. `components/final/AcceptanceFlow.tsx:84-86` relies on a rejected promise that 1.5 turns into a resolved one. After 1.4, the landing and login pages would throw on a DB outage because they resolve the session; they get a `.catch`.
- The recon files `recon/crew-sub-live.md` and `recon/db-health.md` do not exist (only their folders). Live facts above come from SELECTs run today: 95 login_tokens (89 expired), 86 sessions (80 expired or revoked).
- Production baseline before Task 1.2 (measured 05.10.2026, three runs of `/sl/p/demo-epc-k7m2x9q4`): `X-Vercel-Id: fra1::iad1::...`, TTFB 3.62 s, 2.75 s, 2.51 s.

### Task 1.11: lib/format.ts, one locale-aware formatter for numbers, kWp, percent, dates (P0, lane D, 0.75 h)

**Why:** ux-standards (decimals "58.3" and "245.7 kWp" next to "6,5", portfolio tiles) and flows-correctness L4 (document dates computed in UTC print the previous day between 00:00 and 02:00). Tasks 3.3, 3.4, 3.7, 5.5 and 6.1 consume this file, so it lands early and alone.

**Files:**
- Create: `lib/format.ts`, `tests/format.test.ts`.

**Interfaces (Produces):**
```ts
export type AppLocale = "sl" | "de" | "en";
export function asAppLocale(value: string | null | undefined): AppLocale;   // anything else -> "sl"
export const DEFAULT_ZONE = "Europe/Ljubljana";
export function fmtNumber(value: number, locale: string, options?: { decimals?: number; maxDecimals?: number }): string;
export function fmtKwp(kwp: number, locale: string): string;                 // "245,7\u00a0kWp"
export function fmtPct(percent: number, locale: string, decimals?: number): string; // percent is 0..100
export function fmtDate(value: string | Date, locale: string, options?: { style?: "short" | "long"; timeZone?: string }): string;
export function fmtDateTime(value: string | Date, locale: string, timeZone?: string): string;
```
Rules: grouping is always on (matches `formatMoney` in `lib/po-shared.ts:56`); a `yyyy-mm-dd` string is a calendar date and is formatted in UTC so it never shifts; a timestamp is formatted in `timeZone` (default `Europe/Ljubljana`, callers pass `projectZone(country)` from `lib/project-time.ts`); non-finite numbers and unparseable dates return `""`. Pure: no server-only import, usable in client components and PDFs. Existing call sites are NOT migrated here (that is Task 5.5).

  ```ts
  import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
  import { asAppLocale, fmtDate, fmtDateTime, fmtKwp, fmtNumber, fmtPct } from "@/lib/format";

  // Captured from Intl on Node 22.15.0 (ICU 76.1, CLDR 46.0) for sl-SI, de-DE,
  // en-GB. If a Node upgrade changes CLDR, these fail loudly, which is the point:
  // a changed date format on an invoice should be a decision, not a surprise.

  describe("fmtNumber", () => {
    it.each([
      ["sl", 245.7, "245,7"], ["de", 245.7, "245,7"], ["en", 245.7, "245.7"],
      ["sl", 1234.5, "1.234,5"], ["de", 1234.5, "1.234,5"], ["en", 1234.5, "1,234.5"],
      ["sl", 1234567.891, "1.234.567,89"], ["de", 1234567.891, "1.234.567,89"], ["en", 1234567.891, "1,234,567.89"],
      ["sl", -1234.5, "\u22121.234,5"], ["de", -1234.5, "-1.234,5"], ["en", -1234.5, "-1,234.5"],
      ["sl", 0, "0"],
    ])("%s %d", (locale, value, expected) => {
      expect(fmtNumber(value as number, locale as string)).toBe(expected);
    });

    it("fixes the decimals when asked, so a tempo of 6 reads 6,0 next to 6,5", () => {
      expect(fmtNumber(6.5, "sl", { decimals: 1 })).toBe("6,5");
      expect(fmtNumber(6, "sl", { decimals: 1 })).toBe("6,0");
      expect(fmtNumber(6, "de", { decimals: 1 })).toBe("6,0");
      expect(fmtNumber(6, "en", { decimals: 1 })).toBe("6.0");
    });

    it("returns nothing rather than NaN", () => {
      expect(fmtNumber(Number.NaN, "sl")).toBe("");
      expect(fmtNumber(Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY, "sl")).toBe("");
    });
  });

  describe("fmtKwp", () => {
    it.each([
      ["sl", 245.7, "245,7\u00a0kWp"], ["de", 245.7, "245,7\u00a0kWp"], ["en", 245.7, "245.7\u00a0kWp"],
      ["sl", 14.85, "14,85\u00a0kWp"], ["en", 14.85, "14.85\u00a0kWp"],
      ["sl", 1250, "1.250\u00a0kWp"], ["de", 1250, "1.250\u00a0kWp"], ["en", 1250, "1,250\u00a0kWp"],
    ])("%s %d", (locale, value, expected) => {
      expect(fmtKwp(value as number, locale as string)).toBe(expected);
    });
  });

  describe("fmtPct", () => {
    it("takes a 0 to 100 value, the way progressPercent is stored", () => {
      expect(fmtPct(58.3, "sl")).toBe("58\u00a0%");
      expect(fmtPct(58.3, "de")).toBe("58\u00a0%");
      expect(fmtPct(58.3, "en")).toBe("58%");
      expect(fmtPct(58.3, "sl", 1)).toBe("58,3\u00a0%");
      expect(fmtPct(58.3, "en", 1)).toBe("58.3%");
      expect(fmtPct(100, "sl")).toBe("100\u00a0%");
    });
  });

  describe("fmtDate", () => {
    it("short dates per locale", () => {
      expect(fmtDate("2026-10-06", "sl")).toBe("6. 10. 2026");
      expect(fmtDate("2026-10-06", "de")).toBe("06.10.2026");
      expect(fmtDate("2026-10-06", "en")).toBe("06/10/2026");
      expect(fmtDate("2026-01-15", "sl")).toBe("15. 1. 2026");
      expect(fmtDate("2026-01-15", "de")).toBe("15.01.2026");
      expect(fmtDate("2026-01-15", "en")).toBe("15/01/2026");
    });

    it("long dates per locale", () => {
      expect(fmtDate("2026-10-06", "sl", { style: "long" })).toBe("6. oktober 2026");
      expect(fmtDate("2026-10-06", "de", { style: "long" })).toBe("6. Oktober 2026");
      expect(fmtDate("2026-10-06", "en", { style: "long" })).toBe("6 October 2026");
    });

    it("a timestamp at 00:30 site time is that day, not the UTC day before", () => {
      expect(fmtDate("2026-10-05T22:30:00Z", "sl")).toBe("6. 10. 2026");
      expect(fmtDate("2026-10-05T22:30:00Z", "de")).toBe("06.10.2026");
      expect(fmtDate("2026-10-05T22:30:00Z", "sl", { timeZone: "UTC" })).toBe("5. 10. 2026");
    });

    it("a calendar date never shifts, whatever zone is passed", () => {
      expect(fmtDate("2026-10-06", "sl", { timeZone: "America/New_York" })).toBe("6. 10. 2026");
    });

    it("falls back to Slovenian for an unknown locale, and to empty for garbage", () => {
      expect(fmtDate("2026-10-06", "fr")).toBe("6. 10. 2026");
      expect(fmtDate("not a date", "sl")).toBe("");
      expect(asAppLocale("de")).toBe("de");
      expect(asAppLocale(null)).toBe("sl");
    });
  });

  describe("fmtDateTime", () => {
    it("24 hour clock in the site zone", () => {
      expect(fmtDateTime("2026-10-06T12:05:00Z", "sl")).toBe("6. 10. 2026, 14:05");
      expect(fmtDateTime("2026-10-06T12:05:00Z", "de")).toBe("06.10.2026, 14:05");
      expect(fmtDateTime("2026-10-06T12:05:00Z", "en")).toBe("06/10/2026, 14:05");
      expect(fmtDateTime("2026-10-05T22:30:00Z", "sl")).toBe("6. 10. 2026, 00:30");
      expect(fmtDateTime("2026-03-02T07:04:00Z", "sl")).toBe("2. 3. 2026, 08:04");
      expect(fmtDateTime("2026-03-02T07:04:00Z", "de")).toBe("02.03.2026, 08:04");
    });
  });
  ```

- [ ] Create `lib/format.ts`:
  ```ts
  // One place that turns numbers and dates into text, per locale.
  //
  // The screens printed "58.3" and "245.7 kWp" in English decimals beside a
  // Slovenian "6,5", and documents computed dates in UTC, so anything signed
  // between midnight and two in the morning carried yesterday's date. Every new
  // number or date goes through here; Task 5.5 moves the old call sites.
  //
  // Pure on purpose: no server import, so client components, server pages and
  // the PDF renderer share exactly one rule.

  export type AppLocale = "sl" | "de" | "en";

  const INTL: Record<AppLocale, string> = { sl: "sl-SI", de: "de-DE", en: "en-GB" };
  const NBSP = "\u00a0";

  export const DEFAULT_ZONE = "Europe/Ljubljana";

  export function asAppLocale(value: string | null | undefined): AppLocale {
    return value === "de" || value === "en" ? value : "sl";
  }

  /**
   * Grouping is forced, as in formatMoney: Slovenian CLDR leaves four-digit
   * numbers ungrouped ("1250"), and a column of figures wants every thousands
   * mark in the same place.
   */
  export function fmtNumber(
    value: number,
    locale: string,
    options: { decimals?: number; maxDecimals?: number } = {},
  ): string {
    if (!Number.isFinite(value)) return "";
    const { decimals, maxDecimals = 2 } = options;
    return new Intl.NumberFormat(INTL[asAppLocale(locale)], {
      minimumFractionDigits: decimals ?? 0,
      maximumFractionDigits: decimals ?? maxDecimals,
      useGrouping: "always",
    }).format(value);
  }

  /** "245,7 kWp" with a no-break space, so the unit never wraps onto its own line. */
  export function fmtKwp(kwp: number, locale: string): string {
    if (!Number.isFinite(kwp)) return "";
    return `${fmtNumber(kwp, locale, { maxDecimals: 2 })}${NBSP}kWp`;
  }

  /** A 0 to 100 value, which is how progressPercent is stored everywhere. */
  export function fmtPct(percent: number, locale: string, decimals = 0): string {
    if (!Number.isFinite(percent)) return "";
    return new Intl.NumberFormat(INTL[asAppLocale(locale)], {
      style: "percent",
      minimumFractionDigits: decimals,
      maximumFractionDigits: decimals,
    }).format(percent / 100);
  }

  const DATE_ONLY = /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/;

  // Slovenian writes "6. 10. 2026" (Pravopis); German and British English keep
  // two digits, which is what their documents and accountants expect.
  const SHORT: Record<AppLocale, Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions> = {
    sl: { day: "numeric", month: "numeric", year: "numeric" },
    de: { day: "2-digit", month: "2-digit", year: "numeric" },
    en: { day: "2-digit", month: "2-digit", year: "numeric" },
  };
  const LONG: Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions = { day: "numeric", month: "long", year: "numeric" };

  /**
   * A "yyyy-mm-dd" value is a calendar day (an entry date, a deadline, a
   * valid_until) and is formatted in UTC so it can never move. Anything else is
   * an instant and is shown in the given zone, the project's own by default.
   */
  export function fmtDate(
    value: string | Date,
    locale: string,
    options: { style?: "short" | "long"; timeZone?: string } = {},
  ): string {
    const l = asAppLocale(locale);
    const calendarDay = typeof value === "string" && DATE_ONLY.test(value);
    const date =
      value instanceof Date ? value : new Date(calendarDay ? `${value}T00:00:00Z` : value);
    if (Number.isNaN(date.getTime())) return "";
    return new Intl.DateTimeFormat(INTL[l], {
      ...(options.style === "long" ? LONG : SHORT[l]),
      timeZone: calendarDay ? "UTC" : (options.timeZone ?? DEFAULT_ZONE),
    }).format(date);
  }

  export function fmtDateTime(value: string | Date, locale: string, timeZone: string = DEFAULT_ZONE): string {
    const l = asAppLocale(locale);
    const date = value instanceof Date ? value : new Date(value);
    if (Number.isNaN(date.getTime())) return "";
    return new Intl.DateTimeFormat(INTL[l], {
      ...SHORT[l],
      hour: "2-digit",
      minute: "2-digit",
      hourCycle: "h23",
      timeZone,
    }).format(date);
  }
  ```

Add a ledger the test reads, one file per task so parallel lanes never edit the same file. In `tests/messages-parity.test.ts`: change line 2 to `import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs";` and insert after the `SHARED_ON_PURPOSE` set (after line 69):
  ```ts
  /**
   * Keys that knowingly carry the Slovenian string in de and en while a feature
   * is still moving (founder mandate 2026-07-19, Slovenian first). One JSON file
   * per task in tests/translation-debt/, each an array of full keys, so two
   * lanes adding placeholders never edit the same file. Every file is also a
   * DEBT line in CHANGELOG.md, and the translation pass deletes the files.
   */
  function loadTranslationDebt(): Set<string> {
    const dir = path.resolve(__dirname, "translation-debt");
    let files: string[] = [];
    try {
      files = readdirSync(dir).filter((name) => name.endsWith(".json"));
    } catch {
      return new Set();
    }
    const keys = new Set<string>();
    for (const name of files) {
      for (const key of JSON.parse(readFileSync(path.join(dir, name), "utf8")) as string[]) keys.add(key);
    }
    return keys;
  }

  const TRANSLATION_DEBT = loadTranslationDebt();
  ```

*The error type and the loaders:*
- [ ] Create `lib/db-error.ts`:
  ```ts
  /**
   * A read that FAILED, as opposed to a read that found nothing.
   *
   * The two used to be the same thing here. Every loader returned null on a
   * query error and every page turned null into notFound(), so when the free
   * database paused on 05.10.2026 every project link on production told its
   * holder that the link did not exist or had been revoked, for an outage that
   * was ours. A missing row is still null and still a not-found page. A failed
   * read throws this, and app/[locale]/error.tsx answers it with a temporary
   * error and a retry button.
   *
   * Pure, no server-only import: loaders, pages and tests share it.
   */
  export class DataUnavailableError extends Error {
    readonly where: string;

    constructor(where: string, detail?: string) {
      super(`Data unavailable at ${where}${detail ? `: ${detail}` : ""}`);
      this.name = "DataUnavailableError";
      this.where = where;
    }
  }

  export function isDataUnavailable(err: unknown): err is DataUnavailableError {
    return err instanceof Error && err.name === "DataUnavailableError";
  }

  /** Call right after a query with its `error`; throws when the read failed. */
  export function throwIfReadFailed(error: { message: string } | null | undefined, where: string): void {
    if (error) throw new DataUnavailableError(where, error.message);
  }

  /**
   * For a page's catch block around requireProjectActor: an outage goes on to
   * the error page, anything else (not a party, no such project) falls through
   * to the caller's notFound().
   */
  export function rethrowIfUnavailable(err: unknown): void {
    if (isDataUnavailable(err)) throw err;
  }
  ```

*The screens:*
- [ ] `app/[locale]/error.tsx` (client; inside the locale layout, so the intl provider and the CSS are there):
  ```tsx
  "use client";
  import { useEffect, useTransition } from "react";
  import Link from "next/link";
  import { useRouter } from "next/navigation";
  import { useLocale, useTranslations } from "next-intl";
  import { Wordmark } from "@/components/landing/Wordmark";

  // Every unexpected failure under a locale lands here: a failed database read
  // (lib/db-error.ts), a crash in a component, a dropped connection mid render.
  // It never says "your link is invalid": that sentence belongs to a link that
  // really does not exist, and it lives in app/[locale]/p/[token]/not-found.tsx.
  //
  // In production Next hides the message and passes only a digest, which is
  // shown small so a screenshot from a customer can be matched to the log.
  export default function LocaleError({
    error,
    reset,
  }: {
    error: Error & { digest?: string };
    reset: () => void;
  }) {
    const t = useTranslations("errors");
    const locale = useLocale();
    const router = useRouter();
    const [pending, startTransition] = useTransition();

    useEffect(() => {
      console.error(error);
    }, [error]);

    // A server component error needs the server to render again, not only the
    // boundary to reset: refresh first, then reset, in one transition.
    const retry = () =>
      startTransition(() => {
        router.refresh();
        reset();
      });

    return (
      <main className="belin-dark lp">
        <div className="e-grain" aria-hidden />
        <div className="lp-wrap">
          <header className="lp-top">
            <Wordmark href={`/${locale}`} />
          </header>
          <div className="lp-solo">
            <section className="lp-card" role="alert" aria-labelledby="er-title">
              <div className="lp-card-glow" aria-hidden />
              <h1 id="er-title" className="lp-card-title">
                {t("title")}
              </h1>
              <p className="lp-card-sub">{t("body")}</p>
              <div className="er-actions">
                <button type="button" className="lp-submit" onClick={retry} disabled={pending}>
                  {t("retry")}
                </button>
                <Link className="er-link" href={`/${locale}`}>
                  {t("home")}
                </Link>
              </div>
              {error.digest ? <p className="er-code">{t("code", { digest: error.digest })}</p> : null}
            </section>
          </div>
        </div>
      </main>
    );
  }
  ```

### Task 1.5: Server-action error codes survive production builds (P0, lane A, 2.0 h)

**Why:** flows-correctness H1 and i18n-copy I18N-06: in a production build React replaces the message of any error thrown by a server action ("The specific message is omitted in production builds"), so ten components that decode `err.message` as an i18n key show "conflict" or "generic" for every specific problem: a missing declaration, a missing VAT id, an empty incident note.

**Interfaces (Produces):**
```ts
// lib/action-result.ts (no server-only: imported by server actions AND client components)
export type ActionResult<T> = { ok: true; data: T } | { ok: false; code: string };
export const UNEXPECTED = "common.unexpected";
export function codeOf(err: unknown): string;
export class ActionError extends Error { readonly code: string }
export function unwrap<T>(result: ActionResult<T>): T;   // throws ActionError(code) on failure

// lib/action-result-server.ts (server-only)
export async function toResult<T>(work: () => Promise<T>): Promise<ActionResult<T>>;
```
New return types: `savePoDraftAction: ActionResult<{ poId: string }>`, `createSheetAction: ActionResult<{ sheetId: string }>`, `createChangeOrderAction: ActionResult<{ id: string }>`, `generateCompletionReportAction: ActionResult<{ documentId: string }>`, `startAcceptanceAction: ActionResult<{ acceptanceId: string }>`, `generateInvoiceAction: ActionResult<{ warnings: string[] }>`, `createIncidentAction: ActionResult<{ incidentId: string }>`, `createRequestAction: ActionResult<{ requestId: string }>`, every other converted action `ActionResult<null>`.

Design: a component keeps its existing `catch (err)` decoding unchanged. The only client change is `unwrap(await action(...))` at each call site, which throws an `ActionError` whose `message` IS the code, created on the client, so nothing strips it. The codes are exactly the strings lib/data throws today (`po.rejectNote`, `final.err.declaration`, `invoice.errNoVatId`, `incident.err.note`, `common.askOffice`, ...). Anything that is not such a key becomes `common.unexpected` (logged server side with its full message), which every component already maps to its own fallback text. Next's own control-flow errors (redirect, notFound) are rethrown with `unstable_rethrow`.

  ```ts
  // How a server action reports a failure the user can fix.
  //
  // Thrown errors do not survive a production build: React replaces their
  // message with a generic one before it reaches the browser, so every screen
  // that decoded err.message as a message key showed "conflict" for everything
  // on the live site. A RETURNED value is data and arrives intact.
  //
  // No server-only import: actions return ActionResult, and client components
  // call unwrap() on it.

  export type ActionResult<T> = { ok: true; data: T } | { ok: false; code: string };

  /** Anything that is not a known message key: the screen shows its own fallback. */
  export const UNEXPECTED = "common.unexpected";

  // The namespaces lib/data throws keys from. A message outside them is never
  // forwarded, so an internal error text cannot leak to the screen by looking
  // like a key.
  const KEY_NAMESPACES = new Set(["common", "po", "hours", "co", "final", "invoice", "incident", "request"]);
  const KEY = /^[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]*(\.[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*)+$/;

  export function codeOf(err: unknown): string {
    const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : "";
    if (!KEY.test(message)) return UNEXPECTED;
    return KEY_NAMESPACES.has(message.slice(0, message.indexOf("."))) ? message : UNEXPECTED;
  }

  /** Thrown on the CLIENT by unwrap(), so its message is never stripped. */
  export class ActionError extends Error {
    readonly code: string;

    constructor(code: string) {
      super(code);
      this.name = "ActionError";
      this.code = code;
    }
  }

  /**
   * The data of a successful action, or an ActionError carrying the code.
   * Every component already decodes err.message in its catch block; with
   * unwrap() that block keeps working unchanged, in production too.
   */
  export function unwrap<T>(result: ActionResult<T>): T {
    if (result.ok) return result.data;
    throw new ActionError(result.code);
  }
  ```

  ```ts
  import "server-only";
  import { unstable_rethrow } from "next/navigation";
  import { UNEXPECTED, codeOf, type ActionResult } from "@/lib/action-result";

  /**
   * Runs an action body and RETURNS its failure instead of throwing it.
   *
   * redirect() and notFound() are Next's own control flow and must keep
   * propagating, which unstable_rethrow does. A message key from lib/data comes
   * back as its code; anything else is logged here with its full message, where
   * the Vercel log keeps it, and reaches the client only as common.unexpected.
   */
  export async function toResult<T>(work: () => Promise<T>): Promise<ActionResult<T>> {
    try {
      return { ok: true, data: await work() };
    } catch (err) {
      unstable_rethrow(err);
      const code = codeOf(err);
      if (code === UNEXPECTED) console.error("[action] unexpected failure", err);
      return { ok: false, code };
    }
  }
  ```

  ```ts
  // Each RETURNS its failure (lib/action-result.ts): a thrown message key such
  // as final.err.declaration does not survive a production build.

  async function officePerson(): Promise<PersonActor> {
    const actor = await resolveActorFromSession();
    if (!actor || actor.kind !== "person") throw new Error("common.askOffice");
    return actor;
  }

  export async function requestFinalizationAction(projectId: string): Promise<ActionResult<null>> {
    return toResult(async () => {
      await requestFinalization(await officePerson(), projectId);
      return null;
    });
  }

  /**
   * Generate the completion report.
   *
   * Refuses a second run within a minute of the last one. Assembling nine days
   * of photographs is dozens of storage downloads, and a double click on weak
   * LTE would start the whole thing twice and store two documents that differ
   * only by their timestamp.
   */
  export async function generateCompletionReportAction(
    projectId: string,
  ): Promise<ActionResult<{ documentId: string }>> {
    return toResult(async () => {
      const actor = await officePerson();

      const db = createAdminClient();
      const { data: recent } = await db
        .from("generated_documents")
        .select("id, created_at")
        .eq("project_id", projectId)
        .eq("kind", "completion_report")
        .order("created_at", { ascending: false })
        .limit(1)
        .maybeSingle();

      if (recent && Date.now() - Date.parse(recent.created_at) < 60_000) {
        return { documentId: recent.id };
      }

      const result = await generateCompletionReport(actor, projectId);
      return { documentId: result.documentId };
    });
  }
  ```

### Task 1.6: Splash only in the installed app, once per session (P0, lane D, 0.3 h)

**Why:** demo-risk DR-H7, ux-standards H1, landing L5, decision D8: `components/SplashGate.tsx:20` mounts `BelinSplash` without `once`, in the locale layout, so a 4.5 s overlay (z-index 9999, blocks clicks) plays on every hard load, every new tab and every language switch, 6.9 s to content on Fast 3G.

**Files:**
- Modify: `components/SplashGate.tsx` lines 1 to 21; `components/BelinSplash.tsx` lines 53 and 70 (sessionStorage access); `app/globals.css` (append a block).

**Interfaces:** none new. Respects DECISIONS 2026-08-13: the server and the client render the SAME tree; the browser is told apart only by CSS (before hydration) and by an effect (after hydration), never during render.

**Steps:**
- [ ] Append to the end of `app/globals.css` (after the 1.4 block if it has already landed; tonight it usually has not, since the rest of 1.4 is Add order item 4, and 1.4 then appends its block after this one):
  ```css
  /* === 1.6: launch animation only in the installed app === */
  /* The server renders the splash for everyone (DECISIONS 2026-08-13 forbids
     deciding from a client signal in render). CSS decides who sees it before
     any JavaScript runs: a browser tab never does. !important beats the inline
     display:flex on the element in components/BelinSplash.tsx. */
  [data-splash] { display: none !important; }
  @media (display-mode: standalone), (display-mode: fullscreen) {
    [data-splash] { display: flex !important; }
  }
  ```
- [ ] Replace `components/SplashGate.tsx`:
  ```tsx
  "use client";
  import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
  import { BelinSplash } from "@/components/BelinSplash";

  // The launch animation, for the INSTALLED app only, once per session (D8,
  // 2026-10-06): four and a half seconds of logo on every page load read as a
  // slow product in front of a buyer.
  //
  // Who sees it is decided twice, and neither time in render. Before hydration
  // a CSS rule in globals.css hides [data-splash] unless display-mode is
  // standalone. After hydration this effect unmounts it in a browser tab so it
  // stops animating unseen. The server and the client render the same tree, so
  // nothing can desynchronise (the 2026-08-13 hydration lesson, see DECISIONS).
  // Keeping the splash out of product shots is still the capture pipeline's job.
  function isInstalledApp(): boolean {
    if (typeof window === "undefined") return false;
    const standalone =
      typeof window.matchMedia === "function" &&
      (window.matchMedia("(display-mode: standalone)").matches ||
        window.matchMedia("(display-mode: fullscreen)").matches);
    // iOS home-screen apps also expose the older navigator.standalone flag.
    const iosStandalone = (navigator as Navigator & { standalone?: boolean }).standalone === true;
    return standalone || iosStandalone;
  }

  export function SplashGate() {
    const [done, setDone] = useState(false);

    useEffect(() => {
      if (!isInstalledApp()) setDone(true);
    }, []);

    if (done) return null;
    return <BelinSplash once onFinish={() => setDone(true)} />;
  }
  ```
- [ ] `components/BelinSplash.tsx`: wrap the two sessionStorage accesses (a private window or blocked storage throws). Add above the component:
  ```ts
  const SEEN_KEY = "belinSplash";
  function seenThisSession(): boolean {
    try {
      return sessionStorage.getItem(SEEN_KEY) === "1";
    } catch {
      return false;
    }
  }
  function markSeen(): void {
    try {
      sessionStorage.setItem(SEEN_KEY, "1");
    } catch {
      // Storage blocked: the animation may play again next time, which is harmless.
    }
  }
  ```
  Line 53 becomes `if (once && typeof window !== "undefined" && seenThisSession()) {`; line 70 becomes `if (once && typeof window !== "undefined") markSeen();`.
- [ ] `npm run lint` clean.
- [ ] CHANGELOG bullet: "THE LAUNCH ANIMATION PLAYS ONLY IN THE INSTALLED APP, ONCE PER SESSION. A CSS gate on display-mode hides it in every browser tab before JavaScript runs, an effect unmounts it after hydration, and `once` keeps it to the first cold start of a session. Server and client still render the same tree (DECISIONS 2026-08-13)." The D8 line is written at the gate.

  ```ts
  import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
  import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs";
  import path from "node:path";

  // One database serves local, demo and production, and the browser holds the
  // anon key. Two rules keep that safe and both are easy to forget in a new
  // migration, so they are checked here rather than remembered:
  // 1. every table in public has row level security enabled (deny-all for anon;
  //    the app reads with the service role, which bypasses it);
  // 2. every function in public has EXECUTE revoked from public, anon and
  //    authenticated AFTER its last create. DROP plus CREATE, the overload
  //    lesson of DECISIONS 2026-08-12, resets the grants to the open defaults.
  const dir = path.resolve(__dirname, "../supabase/migrations");
  const sources = readdirSync(dir)
    .filter((name) => name.endsWith(".sql"))
    .sort()
    .map((name) => readFileSync(path.join(dir, name), "utf8").replace(/--[^\n]*/g, "").toLowerCase());

  // name -> position of its LAST match, ordered by file then by offset
  function lastPositions(pattern: RegExp): Map<string, number> {
    const out = new Map<string, number>();
    sources.forEach((sql, fileIndex) => {
      for (const match of sql.matchAll(pattern)) {
        const at = fileIndex * 10_000_000 + (match.index ?? 0);
        if ((out.get(match[1]) ?? -1) < at) out.set(match[1], at);
      }
    });
    return out;
  }

  describe("migrations", () => {
    it("enable row level security on every public table", () => {
      const tables = lastPositions(/create table (?:if not exists )?public\.([a-z_]+)/g);
      const secured = lastPositions(/alter table public\.([a-z_]+) enable row level security/g);
      expect([...tables.keys()].filter((name) => !secured.has(name))).toEqual([]);
    });

    it("close EXECUTE to public, anon and authenticated after the last create of every public function", () => {
      const created = lastPositions(/create (?:or replace )?function public\.([a-z_]+)\s*\(/g);
      const revoked = lastPositions(
        /revoke execute on function public\.([a-z_]+)\s*\([^)]*\)\s+from\s+public\s*,\s*anon\s*,\s*authenticated/g,
      );
      const open = [...created].filter(([name, at]) => (revoked.get(name) ?? -1) < at).map(([name]) => name);
      expect(open).toEqual([]);
    });
  });
  ```

  ```ts
  import "server-only";
  import { createAdminClient } from "@/lib/supabase/admin";
  import { LOGIN_RATE_MAX } from "@/lib/auth-core";

  /**
   * True when this person already holds LOGIN_RATE_MAX live, unused login links.
   * Shared by the login form and the crew claim, so both doors flood nobody.
   * Fails CLOSED: an unknown count must not become an unlimited sender.
   */
  export async function loginRateExceeded(personId: string): Promise<boolean> {
    const { count, error } = await createAdminClient()
      .from("login_tokens")
      .select("id", { count: "exact", head: true })
      .eq("person_id", personId)
      .is("used_at", null)
      .gt("expires_at", new Date().toISOString());
    if (error) return true;
    return (count ?? 0) >= LOGIN_RATE_MAX;
  }
  ```

  ```ts
  /**
   * A claim address normalised the way people.email is stored (trimmed,
   * lowercased; a database constraint enforces lowercase since 2026-10-06), or
   * null when it cannot be an address. Matching is EXACT from here on: the old
   * ILIKE lookup treated _ and % as wildcards.
   */
  export function normalizeClaimEmail(raw: string): string | null {
    const email = raw.trim().toLowerCase();
    if (email.length < 5 || email.length > 254) return null;
    if (/[\s\u0000-\u001f\u007f]/.test(email)) return null;
    const at = email.indexOf("@");
    if (at < 1 || at !== email.lastIndexOf("@") || at === email.length - 1) return null;
    if (!email.slice(at + 1).includes(".")) return null;
    return email;
  }

  export type ClaimDecision =
    | { kind: "existing"; personId: string; sendTo: string }
    | { kind: "create" }
    | { kind: "refuse" };

  /**
   * What a claim does with the person an address already belongs to. The link
   * always goes to the address the ROW holds: the claim proves you are on the
   * site, the mailbox proves you are you, and only the owner reads that mailbox.
   */
  export function decideClaim(
    existing: { id: string; email: string | null; disabled_at: string | null } | null,
  ): ClaimDecision {
    if (!existing) return { kind: "create" };
    if (existing.disabled_at || !existing.email) return { kind: "refuse" };
    return { kind: "existing", personId: existing.id, sendTo: existing.email };
  }
  ```

### Task 1.10: Signed photo URLs never served expired (P1, lane A, 0.4 h)

**Why:** flows-correctness H11: `lib/storage.ts:129-142` and `:154-167` cache 3600 s signed URLs with `unstable_cache({ revalidate: 3000 })`, and Next serves a stale entry once while it revalidates in the background, so after an hour idle (the founder opens the dashboard in the morning and presents in the afternoon) the first view shows broken photos. New: one failed signing call caches an empty map for 50 minutes (`if (error || !data) return {};` inside the cached function).

**Files:**
- Create: `lib/storage-shared.ts`, `tests/storage-shared.test.ts`.
- Modify: `lib/storage.ts` lines 3 to 5 (imports), 124 to 148 (`signPaths`, `getSignedPhotoUrlMap`), 150 to 186 (`signDocPaths`, `getSignedDocUrlMap`).

**Interfaces:**
- Produces in `lib/storage-shared.ts` (pure): `SIGNED_URL_TTL_S = 7200`, `SIGN_BUCKET_MS = 1_800_000`, `signBucket(nowMs: number): number`.
- `getSignedPhotoUrlMap(paths)` and `getSignedDocUrlMap(paths)` keep their signatures.

**Steps:**
- [ ] Test first, `tests/storage-shared.test.ts`:
  ```ts
  import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
  import { SIGNED_URL_TTL_S, SIGN_BUCKET_MS, signBucket } from "@/lib/storage-shared";

  describe("signed URL caching", () => {
    it("serves no URL with less than ninety minutes left", () => {
      // A cached batch is reused at most until its bucket ends, so the oldest
      // URL a page can receive was signed SIGN_BUCKET_MS ago.
      expect(SIGNED_URL_TTL_S * 1000 - SIGN_BUCKET_MS).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(90 * 60 * 1000);
    });

    it("keeps one key for half an hour and changes it after", () => {
      const start = Date.UTC(2026, 9, 6, 9, 0, 0);
      expect(signBucket(start)).toBe(signBucket(start + SIGN_BUCKET_MS - 1));
      expect(signBucket(start + SIGN_BUCKET_MS)).toBe(signBucket(start) + 1);
    });
  });
  ```
- [ ] `lib/storage-shared.ts`:
  ```ts
  // Signed URLs are cached so a page that refreshes live hands the browser the
  // SAME URLs and its image cache hits. The cache key carries a half-hour
  // bucket, so no batch is reused for longer than that, and the URLs live two
  // hours: whatever a page receives still has at least ninety minutes.
  //
  // Before 2026-10-06 the key had no bucket and the entries revalidated after
  // 50 minutes with stale-while-revalidate, so the first view after an hour idle
  // was served URLs that had already expired: broken photos on stage.

  export const SIGNED_URL_TTL_S = 2 * 60 * 60;
  export const SIGN_BUCKET_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000;

  export function signBucket(nowMs: number): number {
    return Math.floor(nowMs / SIGN_BUCKET_MS);
  }
  ```
- [ ] `lib/storage.ts`: import `{ SIGNED_URL_TTL_S, SIGN_BUCKET_MS, signBucket } from "@/lib/storage-shared"`. Replace lines 124 to 148:
  ```ts
  // Cached per half-hour bucket (lib/storage-shared.ts explains the numbers).
  // A failure THROWS inside the cached function: unstable_cache stores a
  // returned value, and a returned {} hid every photo for fifty minutes after a
  // single storage hiccup. A throw is not cached; the wrapper answers {} for
  // this one render only.
  const signPaths = unstable_cache(
    async (paths: string[], bucket: number): Promise<Record<string, string>> => {
      void bucket; // part of the cache key only
      const db = createAdminClient();
      const { data, error } = await db.storage.from("photos").createSignedUrls(paths, SIGNED_URL_TTL_S);
      if (error || !data) throw new Error(`Could not sign photos: ${error?.message ?? "no data"}`);
      const map: Record<string, string> = {};
      for (const d of data) {
        if (d.path && d.signedUrl) map[d.path] = d.signedUrl;
      }
      return map;
    },
    ["signed-photos-v2"],
    { revalidate: SIGN_BUCKET_MS / 1000 },
  );

  // (keep the existing comment of lines 144 to 147)
  export async function getSignedPhotoUrlMap(paths: string[]): Promise<Record<string, string>> {
    if (paths.length === 0) return {};
    try {
      // Sorted so the same set produces the same cache key regardless of order.
      return await signPaths([...paths].sort(), signBucket(Date.now()));
    } catch (err) {
      console.error("[storage] photo signing failed", err);
      return {};
    }
  }
  ```
  and the same shape for `signDocPaths` (key `["signed-docs-v2"]`, bucket `"docs"`, message `Could not sign documents`) and `getSignedDocUrlMap`, keeping THE RULE comment of lines 169 to 182 verbatim.

The documented guard is `if (!cronSecret || authHeader !== \`Bearer ${cronSecret}\`) return 401`.

  ```ts
  import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
  import { isCronAuthorized } from "@/lib/cron-shared";

  const SECRET = "s3cret-value-of-forty-three-characters-xyz1";

  describe("isCronAuthorized", () => {
  ```

  ```ts
  import { timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";

  /**
   * Vercel sends CRON_SECRET as "Authorization: Bearer <secret>" on every cron
   * invocation (vercel.com/docs/cron-jobs/manage-cron-jobs, read 2026-10-05).
   * Fails closed: no secret, or one shorter than the 16 characters Vercel
   * recommends, means nobody is authorized, not everybody.
   */
  export function isCronAuthorized(header: string | null, secret: string | undefined): boolean {
    if (!secret || secret.length < 16 || !header) return false;
    const expected = Buffer.from(`Bearer ${secret}`);
    const given = Buffer.from(header);
    return given.length === expected.length && timingSafeEqual(given, expected);
  }
  ```

  ```ts
  import "server-only";
  import { createAdminClient } from "@/lib/supabase/admin";
  import { emitEvent, emitEventDeferred, type EmitEventInput } from "@/lib/notify";
  import { expiryState, EXPIRY_WARN_DAYS, type ExpiryState } from "@/lib/vault-shared";

  export interface ReminderDoc {
    id: string;
    title: string | null;
    validUntil: string | null;
    state: ExpiryState;
  }

  /**
   * Tells the subcontractor once, per document, per threshold, that a
   * certificate is running out. Moved here from lib/data/epc-dashboard.ts on
   * 2026-10-06 so the daily cron uses the SAME claim as the dashboard: inserting
   * the document_reminders row IS the claim, the unique index from
   * 20260812102000 makes exactly one caller win, and only the winner notifies.
   * The dashboard and the cron can therefore both run it without ever sending
   * twice. Returns how many reminders this call claimed.
   */
  export async function warnAboutExpiries(
    projectId: string,
    docs: ReminderDoc[],
    emit: (input: EmitEventInput) => Promise<void> = emitEventDeferred,
  ): Promise<number> {
    const due = docs.filter((doc) => doc.state === "expiringSoon" || doc.state === "expired");
    if (due.length === 0) return 0;

    const db = createAdminClient();
    let claimed = 0;

    for (const doc of due) {
      const threshold = doc.state === "expired" ? 0 : EXPIRY_WARN_DAYS;
      const { error } = await db
        .from("document_reminders")
        .insert({ document_id: doc.id, days_before: threshold });

      // 23505: somebody already claimed this threshold. The common path.
      if (error) continue;
      claimed += 1;

      await emit({
        projectId,
        kind: "document_expiring",
        actorPerson: null,
        payload: { title: doc.title ?? "", date: doc.validUntil ?? "" },
      });
    }
    return claimed;
  }

  const LIVE_STATUSES = ["draft", "active", "paused", "reviewing"];

  /**
   * Every document in the product that is expiring or expired, reminded through
   * the newest live project its company works on. A company on no live project
   * is skipped and counted: there is no project to file the reminder against.
   */
  export async function runExpiryReminders(
    now: Date = new Date(),
  ): Promise<{ due: number; warned: number; skippedNoProject: number }> {
    const db = createAdminClient();
    const horizon = new Date(now.getTime() + EXPIRY_WARN_DAYS * 86_400_000).toISOString().slice(0, 10);

    const { data: rows, error } = await db
      .from("documents")
      .select("id, org_id, title, valid_until")
      .not("valid_until", "is", null)
      .lte("valid_until", horizon);
    if (error) throw new Error(`documents read failed: ${error.message}`);

    const due = (rows ?? [])
      .map((row) => ({
        id: row.id,
        orgId: row.org_id,
        title: row.title,
        validUntil: row.valid_until,
        state: expiryState(row.valid_until, now),
      }))
      .filter((doc) => doc.state === "expiringSoon" || doc.state === "expired");
    if (due.length === 0) return { due: 0, warned: 0, skippedNoProject: 0 };

    const { data: projects, error: projectError } = await db
      .from("projects")
      .select("id, sub_org_id, created_at")
      .in("sub_org_id", [...new Set(due.map((doc) => doc.orgId))])
      .in("status", LIVE_STATUSES)
      .order("created_at", { ascending: false });
    if (projectError) throw new Error(`projects read failed: ${projectError.message}`);

    const projectByOrg = new Map<string, string>();
    for (const project of projects ?? []) {
      if (project.sub_org_id && !projectByOrg.has(project.sub_org_id)) {
        projectByOrg.set(project.sub_org_id, project.id);
      }
    }

    let warned = 0;
    let skippedNoProject = 0;
    for (const doc of due) {
      const projectId = projectByOrg.get(doc.orgId);
      if (!projectId) {
        skippedNoProject += 1;
        continue;
      }
      // Awaited, not deferred: the cron's response is the moment the work must be done.
      warned += await warnAboutExpiries(projectId, [doc], emitEvent);
    }
    return { due: due.length, warned, skippedNoProject };
  }
  ```

  ```ts
  /**
   * The same write as persistDeemed, for every project at once, from the daily
   * cron (D20, 2026-10-06): "the clock approved your hours" must reach the
   * subcontractor even when nobody opens the hours page. The status condition
   * makes it race-free with persistDeemed: a sheet flips, and notifies, once.
   */
  export async function persistDeemedAll(now: Date = new Date()): Promise<number> {
    const { data, error } = await createAdminClient()
      .from("hour_sheets")
      .update({ status: "deemed_approved" })
      .eq("status", "submitted")
      .lte("deadline_at", now.toISOString())
      .select("id, number, project_id");
    if (error) throw new Error(`deemed approval failed: ${error.message}`);

    for (const row of data ?? []) {
      await emitEvent({
        projectId: row.project_id,
        kind: "hours_deemed_approved",
        actorPerson: null,
        payload: { number: String(row.number) },
      });
    }
    return data?.length ?? 0;
  }
  ```

  ```ts
  import "server-only";
  import { createAdminClient } from "@/lib/supabase/admin";
  import { persistDeemedAll } from "@/lib/data/hours";
  import { runExpiryReminders } from "@/lib/data/expiry-reminders";
  import { sweepAbandonedPlans } from "@/lib/data/plan-imports";

  export type JobResult =
    | { ok: true; ms: number; result: Record<string, number> }
    | { ok: false; ms: number; error: string };

  // Each job runs on its own: one failing must not stop the others, and the
  // response says exactly which one failed. Every job is idempotent, because
  // Vercel may skip a run or deliver it twice.
  async function job(work: () => Promise<Record<string, number>>): Promise<JobResult> {
    const start = Date.now();
    try {
      // Awaited first: an object literal evaluates its fields in order, so
      // writing ms before an inline await would always measure zero.
      const result = await work();
      return { ok: true, ms: Date.now() - start, result };
    } catch (err) {
      const error = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
      console.error(`[cron] job failed: ${error}`);
      return { ok: false, ms: Date.now() - start, error };
    }
  }

  /**
   * Login links live fifteen minutes and sessions thirty days; their rows were
   * never deleted. A day of grace keeps yesterday's rows for diagnosing a
   * "my link did not work" call.
   */
  export async function pruneAuthRows(now: Date = new Date()): Promise<{ loginTokens: number; sessions: number }> {
    const cutoff = new Date(now.getTime() - 86_400_000).toISOString();
    const db = createAdminClient();

    const tokens = await db.from("login_tokens").delete().lt("expires_at", cutoff).select("id");
    if (tokens.error) throw new Error(`login_tokens: ${tokens.error.message}`);

    const expired = await db.from("sessions").delete().lt("expires_at", cutoff).select("id");
    if (expired.error) throw new Error(`sessions: ${expired.error.message}`);

    const revoked = await db.from("sessions").delete().eq("revoked", true).lt("created_at", cutoff).select("id");
    if (revoked.error) throw new Error(`sessions revoked: ${revoked.error.message}`);

    return {
      loginTokens: tokens.data?.length ?? 0,
      sessions: (expired.data?.length ?? 0) + (revoked.data?.length ?? 0),
    };
  }

  export async function runDailyJobs(now: Date = new Date()) {
    const db = createAdminClient();
    const jobs = {
      // One real query a day keeps a free Supabase project from pausing after
      // seven quiet days, which is what took the whole app down on 05.10.2026.
      keepAlive: await job(async () => {
        const { count, error } = await db.from("projects").select("id", { count: "exact", head: true });
        if (error) throw new Error(error.message);
        return { projects: count ?? 0 };
      }),
      deemedApprovals: await job(async () => ({ sheets: await persistDeemedAll(now) })),
      expiryReminders: await job(() => runExpiryReminders(now)),
      prune: await job(() => pruneAuthRows(now)),
      abandonedPlans: await job(async () => sweepAbandonedPlans()),
    };
    return { ok: Object.values(jobs).every((j) => j.ok), at: now.toISOString(), jobs };
  }
  ```

  ```ts
  import type { NextRequest } from "next/server";
  import { isCronAuthorized } from "@/lib/cron-shared";
  import { runDailyJobs } from "@/lib/jobs/daily";

  export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";
  export const maxDuration = 60;

  // Registered in vercel.json, once a day (the Hobby limit). Vercel calls it
  // with "Authorization: Bearer <CRON_SECRET>"; anyone else gets 401.
  export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
    if (!isCronAuthorized(request.headers.get("authorization"), process.env.CRON_SECRET)) {
      return new Response("Unauthorized", { status: 401 });
    }
    const report = await runDailyJobs();
    return Response.json(report, {
      status: report.ok ? 200 : 500,
      headers: { "Cache-Control": "no-store" },
    });
  }
  ```
